Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FORCEPS, GOUGE, ANGULAR, ORTHOPAEDIC 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope — Dimensions and other requirements for gouge forceps, angular type, used in orthopaedic 
surgery. 

2. Material 

2.1 Arms — Stainless steel having the following composition: 

Percent 
Carbon 0*35 to 0*45 

Silicon I *0 Max 

Manganese 1*0 Max 

Chromium 12-5 to 145 

Nickel hO Max 

Sulphur 0-03 Max 

Phosphorus 0*03 Mox 

2.2 Springs — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30Crl3 of Schedule V of IS: 1570-1961 ^Schedules 
for wrought steels for general engineering purposes'. 

2.3 Screws — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 22Crl3 of Schedule V of IS : 1570-1961. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

4. Workmanship 

4.1 The forceps shall be free fromttt^h lodges, pits, burrs, cracks and blemishes of an/ kind. 

4.2 Th4 cutting edges shall be sharpi^if vnlform. 

43 When the jaws are closed, the cuttltig edges shaH meet evenly. 

4.4 The joints shall have no undue play, 

4.5 The spring action shall be smooth. It shall be neither too hard nor too slack. 

4.6 The compound action shall be smooth and free from jerks. 

5. Heat Treatment — The arms shall be hardened and tempered to 520 to 600 HV, the springs to 
380 to 420 HV and the screws to 290 to 320 HY. 

6. Finish — T^e forceps shall be finished smooth, passivated and polished bright. 

?• Tests 

7.1 Performance Test — Cut a piece of rib of a fully grown goat or sheep five times with the instrument. 
Each time the instrument shall cut the rib evenly in one bite without any undue resistance, and cutting 
edges shall not show any sign of damage. 

7.2 Load Closure Test —Apply a compressive force of 15 ± 2 N ( l'5 ±0*2 kgf approximately ) at the ends 
of the handles. The cutting edges shall meet evenly after the test. 

7.3 Corrosion Res/stance Test — Scrub the Instrument with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the instrument, immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and wash with fresh water or wet cotton wool. 

The copper sulphate solution shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate (CUSO4.5H2O) 4-0 g 

Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) (spgr 1-84) 10*0 g 

Distilled water [see IS : 1070-1960 Specification for 90'0 ml 

water, distilled quality (rev/sed)] 

There shall be no red stains or spots on the instrument, but dulling of the polished surface may be 
permitted, . 

a. Marlcing — The forceps shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) Country of origin. 

8.1 ISI Certification Aiarkfng — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi I. 

9. Paclcing ~ As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
